_comment: Projects the corpus job parses, pinned by commit so a run is reproducible and a red build
is always our regression rather than somebody else refactoring overnight.
Nothing here is vendored. The job clones each project at the pinned sha and throws it away,
so this repository stays MIT and redistributes nobody else code. Licences are recorded
because the choice was deliberate, not because a clone needs one.
Chosen for variety of failure mode rather than for fame: heavy generics, one enormous file,
an interface-first architecture, and deep inheritance.
minNodes is a floor measured on the pinned sha and set below it. Parsers return a partial
graph instead of throwing, so a collapse in this number is what a broken parser looks like.
Raise a floor when the measured number rises. Never lower one to make a red build green:
re-pin the sha instead, and say in the commit why the project got smaller.

projects.name: guava
projects.why: Generics at their most brutal. The best available stress test for rawType() and the stdlib skip-list in ClassDiagramParser.

projects.name: picocli
projects.why: One file of roughly fifteen thousand lines. Exercises the single-file path at a size no fixture reaches.

projects.name: junit5
projects.why: Interface-first extension architecture, and the one project here whose diagram is worth looking at.

projects.name: jackson-databind
projects.why: Deep inheritance chains, and already a dependency of this project, so a regression here reaches us directly. Note the 3.x package move to tools.jackson.databind.
